subject: botany_2
question_text: Compare the pH of guard cells during the opening and closing of stomata.

insider_note: Two lines, opposite directions. Get the opening direction right and the closing one follows.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: During opening
steps.margin_note: Direction plus the ion that causes it. Three lines.
lines: The pH of the guard cells INCREASES during the
H+ ions are pumped out as K+ ions enter, so the
steps.why: Protons leaving is what makes the inside less acidic, so the pH rise is a direct consequence of the ion pump that opens the pore.
common_mistakes: Saying the pH falls on opening. It RISES.
Giving the direction with no cause. The proton efflux is what makes it rise.
steps.memory_tip: Protons out means acid out means pH up.

steps.label: During closing
steps.margin_note: The mirror of the opening line. Three lines.

lines.text: pH up on opening, down on closing

lines: The pH of the guard cells DECREASES during the
H+ ions return as K+ ions leave.
steps.why: Closing reverses the same pump, so the pH must move the other way.
common_mistakes: Giving the same direction for both. They are opposites.
Confusing pH with concentration of potassium. Potassium leaves; the pH falls.
steps.memory_tip: Reverse the pump and you reverse the pH.
